moduleName: Remote Recruitment, HR Impersonation & Onboarding Scams

questions.questionText: What is the primary goal of scammers running fake remote job outreach campaigns?

options.text: To help workers improve their resumes.
To steal Personally Identifiable Information (PII), commit identity theft, or execute equipment check fraud.
To provide free laptops to remote contractors.
To test local internet connection speeds.

questions.explanation: Fake job scams harvest PII and run advance-fee equipment check schemes (Ravenelle et al., 2022).

questions.questionText: A legitimate international company will routinely hire remote employees for high-paying roles based purely on a 10-minute text conversation on Telegram without any video or voice interviews.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Text-only "interviews" on anonymous messaging apps are major indicators of recruitment fraud.

questions.questionText: You are hired for a remote position. The company mails you a $3,000 check and instructs you to deposit it, keep $500 as a sign-on bonus, and wire $2,500 to an "approved software vendor." What should you do?

options.text: Wire the $2,500 immediately.
Recognize this as a fake check scam; do not wire any money and report the fraudulent offer.
Keep the full $3,000 and buy personal items.
Mail $2,500 in cash to the vendor.

questions.explanation: Fake check scams rely on victims wiring real money before the bank identifies the deposited check as fraudulent.

questions.questionText: Which of the following details indicate that a remote job offer may be fraudulent? (Select TWO)

options.text: The recruiter asks for your online banking login credentials to set up direct deposit.
The job offer comes from an email address using a lookalike domain (careers-google-jobs.com).
The interview was conducted via a scheduled video conference with HR personnel.
The job contract clearly states working hours and payment terms.

questions.explanation: Requesting bank passwords and using lookalike email domains indicate recruitment fraud.

questions.questionText: Legitimate employers require new hires to pay application fees or background check fees upfront via cryptocurrency.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Legitimate employers cover hiring and background check costs; demanding crypto payments indicates fraud.

questions.questionText: What type of sensitive data is targeted during pre-employment PII harvesting scams?

options.text: Public social media posts
Passport scans, government ID numbers, home addresses, and bank account numbers
Favorite movie genres
Public software documentation

questions.explanation: PII is harvested to commit identity theft, open fraudulent credit lines, or breach accounts.

questions.questionText: You receive an email from hr@microsoft-remote-careers.site inviting you to apply for an administrative position. How can you verify if this domain belongs to Microsoft?

options.text: Trust it because it has "Microsoft" in the name.
Check Microsoft's official corporate website (microsoft.com/careers) or contact their verified talent team directly.
Reply to the email asking if they are real.
Click all links in the email footer.

questions.explanation: Always cross-reference job outreach domains against official corporate career portals.

questions.questionText: How does the fake equipment check scam operate?

options.text: The employer sends real laptops that do not work.
The employer sends a counterfeit check, instructs the worker to wire money to a fake vendor, and the check bounces later.
The employer steals the worker's home furniture.
The employer installs free antivirus software on the worker's phone.

questions.explanation: The counterfeit check bounces after the victim has already transferred real personal funds to the scammer.

questions.questionText: Scammers frequently copy authentic logos, employee photos, and executive names from LinkedIn to create convincing fake recruiter profiles.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Copied branding assets build false credibility and lower applicant vigilance.

questions.questionText: What is the primary risk of uploading your full unredacted driver's license or passport scan to an unverified job portal?

options.text: It consumes cloud storage space.
It enables threat actors to execute identity theft, register fraudulent accounts, or conduct loan fraud in your name.
It changes your computer screen brightness.
It automatically cancels your driver's license.

questions.explanation: Unredacted government IDs are primary assets used in identity fraud and unauthorized account creation.
